steps.intent: As humanitarian co-penholder alongside Germany and Kuwait, Belgium's primary objective is to preserve the vital cross-border aid mechanism established under resolution 2165 (2014) for a full 12-month period, ensuring continuous, life-saving assistance reaches over 4 million civilians in need in north-western and north-eastern Syria through Bab al-Salam, Bab al-Hawa, and Al Yarubiyah. The most difficult negotiation points are expected to be the mandate duration and the retention of the Al Yarubiyah crossing in the north-east, which the Russian Federation strongly opposes, demanding a shorter six-month extension and the reduction of crossings to only two in the north-west under the argument of Syrian state sovereignty and a shift toward cross-line operations.

messages.China: China has always maintained that humanitarian assistance to Syria must fully respect Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity, and that the cross-border mechanism is an exceptional and temporary arrangement that must be adjusted to reflect changes on the ground. A twelve-month renewal and the inclusion of crossings where the situation has fundamentally changed do not align with current realities or the consent of the host Government. We urge the co-penholders to engage in extensive consultations, accommodate the core concerns of all parties, and avoid pushing a divisive draft to a vote.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire fully supports the draft resolution prepared by the co-penholders, as renewing the cross-border humanitarian mechanism remains an indispensable lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians in desperate need. We commend the co-penholders' constructive efforts to address Council concerns, including the exclusion of Al-Ramtha and the inclusion of an independent review. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and unity to ensure the renewal of this critical humanitarian mandate without interruption.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic fully supports the draft resolution presented by the co-penholders Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait. Ensuring uninterrupted, vital cross-border humanitarian assistance for millions of civilians in north-western and north-eastern Syria must remain the Council's utmost priority. We commend the co-penholders for their balanced approach and urge all Council members to preserve this critical humanitarian lifeline.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism to ensure critical aid continues reaching Syrian civilians in dire need. However, to avoid another damaging division and veto in the Council, we urge the penholders to demonstrate maximum flexibility and engage constructively with all members to bridge remaining differences on the modalities and crossings. Council unity must be preserved above all when addressing the humanitarian suffering of the Syrian people.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait, which reflects the clear humanitarian needs identified on the ground and by the Secretary-General. Preserving cross-border authorization for twelve months across the three vital crossings—Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam, and Al Yarubiyah—is an indispensable lifeline for over four million civilians in north-western and north-eastern Syria. We stand firmly behind the co-penholders and urge the Council not to undermine the operational capacity of the United Nations to deliver life-saving assistance.
messages.Germany: As co-penholder alongside Belgium and Kuwait, Germany fully supports this draft text. Reauthorizing the cross-border mechanism for 12 months via Bab al-Salam, Bab al-Hawa, and Al Yarubiyah is an indispensable humanitarian lifeline for millions of civilians in north-western and north-eastern Syria who cannot be reached by other means. We urge all Council members to maintain a strictly humanitarian focus and support this balanced text without undermining the UN's operational capacity to save lives.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia fully supports the draft resolution prepared by the co-penholders, as renewing the cross-border humanitarian mechanism is an indispensable lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians in dire need. In line with our core principle to always 'put people first', political differences must not impede the delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance. We commend Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait for their tireless efforts and urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and work towards unity to avoid a humanitarian catastrophe.
messages.Kuwait: As a co-penholder alongside Belgium and Germany, Kuwait fully supports the draft resolution as circulated. The cross-border mechanism remains an irreplaceable humanitarian lifeline for over four million Syrians in desperate need, particularly in the north-west and north-east as winter sets in. We urge all Council members to prioritize purely humanitarian considerations, preserve Council unity, and adopt this vital text to renew the authorization for Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam, and Al Yarubiyah for twelve months.
messages.Peru: Peru expresses its full support for the draft resolution presented by the co-penholders Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait to renew the cross-border humanitarian mechanism. Cross-border assistance remains an indispensable lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians whose lives depend on the sustained delivery of aid. We urge all Council members to prioritize the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian people and work constructively towards consensus so that this vital mechanism can continue without interruption.
messages.Poland: Poland extends its full support to the draft resolution presented by the co-penholders Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait. Renewing the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months across Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam, and Al Yarubiyah is an absolute necessity to prevent an even greater humanitarian catastrophe. We urge all Council members to prioritize the life-saving needs of millions of Syrian civilians and support this text without compromise.
messages.Russian Federation: The co-sponsors' draft ignores the realities on the ground in Syria, where the Syrian Government has restored control over large parts of its territory, rendering border points like Al Yarubiyah completely unjustified and obsolete. Resolution 2165 was designed as an emergency, temporary mechanism, not an indefinite infringement on Syrian sovereignty. The Russian Federation cannot accept a twelve-month extension or the inclusion of Al Yarubiyah; we can only support a renewal limited to the two Turkish border crossings (Bab al-Salam and Bab al-Hawa) for a period of six months.
messages.South Africa: South Africa views the cross-border humanitarian mechanism as an indispensable lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians and supports the renewal of the mandate. However, we urge the co-penholders to actively pursue consensus among all Council members to avoid an impasse and ensure that life-saving aid is not disrupted. Humanitarian aid must remain strictly depoliticized, with enhanced efforts to scale up cross-line assistance in full respect of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution prepared by the humanitarian penholders, which represents a vital and carefully calibrated response to the acute humanitarian needs across northern Syria. Reauthorizing the three crossings—Bab al-Salam, Bab al-Hawa, and Al Yarubiyah—for a full twelve months is an indispensable minimum, particularly given the critical medical needs in the north-east and ongoing hostilities in the north-west. We urge all Council members to support this text without dilution, as there is currently no viable alternative to cross-border delivery to sustain millions of vulnerable civilians.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the co-penholders' draft resolution to reauthorize the vital cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months through the Bab al-Salam, Bab al-Hawa, and Al Yarubiyah crossings. Cross-border aid is an irreplaceable lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians facing relentless attacks by the Assad regime and Russia, and maintaining Al Yarubiyah is essential for delivering life-saving medical supplies to the northeast. We urge all Council members to support this compromise text and resist any attempts to further erode or compromise this critical humanitarian mandate.

steps.summary: As co-penholder alongside Germany and Kuwait, Belgium maintained the draft resolution without changes, prioritizing the humanitarian imperative of preserving an indispensable lifeline of three border crossings for twelve months to reach over four million civilians in need. Requests by the Russian Federation and China to reduce the mandate to six months and exclude Al Yarubiyah were rejected as they would deprive vulnerable populations in north-eastern Syria of vital medical supplies and assistance. Thirteen Council members support the text, while the Russian Federation and China are expected to cast negative votes.

before.Belgium:
I have the honour to speak on behalf of the three co-penholders of the humanitarian file on Syria: Germany, Kuwait and my own country, Belgium.

For months, our three delegations have worked tirelessly, transparently and in close consultation with all members of the Security Council to ensure the continuation of life-saving humanitarian assistance to the millions of Syrian men, women and children who depend on it for their survival. 

The text before us today is purely humanitarian. As the Secretary-General and the Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs have consistently reminded this Council, cross-border humanitarian assistance remains an indispensable lifeline. There is simply no viable alternative to reaching people in need in northern Syria, where over four million civilians rely directly on cross-border deliveries for food, clean water, medical supplies and shelter. 

In drafting this resolution, the co-penholders have made extraordinary efforts to take into account the concerns expressed by all Council members. We have listened, we have accommodated, and we have adapted the text to the realities on the ground, including by reducing the authorized border crossings from four to three. However, we cannot compromise on the humanitarian imperative. Closing additional crossings or failing to renew this mandate would have devastating, catastrophic consequences for millions of innocent civilians, particularly as winter sets in and violence escalates.

This is not a political text; it is a moral and humanitarian duty. We urge all members of the Security Council to put the lives of Syrian civilians first and to vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation will vote against the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait. 

From the very beginning of the consultations on this file, our delegation made our principled approach completely clear. The cross-border humanitarian mechanism was introduced in 2014 by resolution 2165 as an exceptional, temporary measure at a time when the Syrian Government lacked control over vast swathes of its territory and there were no alternative means of delivering aid. Today, the situation on the ground has changed radically. Syrian authorities have re-established control over the majority of the country's territory. 

Any humanitarian mechanism must strictly respect the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, in full compliance with the Guiding Principles of humanitarian assistance set out in General Assembly resolution 46/182, which require the consent of the host State. Cross-border assistance cannot be an indefinite substitute for deliveries from within the country across conflict lines in coordination with Damascus. 

The co-sponsors have stubbornly ignored these realities. Our compromises were disregarded, including our proposal to extend the mechanism for six months and to focus on the two operational border crossings in the north-west, Bab al-Salam and Bab al-Hawa, while phasing out crossings like Al Yarubiyah where delivery can and must be arranged from Damascus. By insisting on maintaining three crossings for a year and pushing an unviable text to a vote, the co-sponsors have deliberately chosen confrontation over consensus and bear full responsibility for the failure of this draft.

after.China:
China has always attached great importance to the humanitarian situation in Syria and has consistently supported the United Nations and other international agencies in scaling up humanitarian relief for the Syrian people. China has actively and constructively participated in the consultations on the draft resolution and worked tirelessly with all parties to seek a consensus-based solution.

China has always maintained that the delivery of humanitarian relief to Syria must strictly respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, listen attentively to the views of the Syrian Government, and strictly abide by the Charter of the United Nations and the guiding principles for United Nations humanitarian emergency assistance set out in General Assembly resolution 46/182.

The Syrian Government bears primary responsibility for improving the humanitarian situation in Syria. In addressing the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people, priority should be given to providing humanitarian assistance from inside Syria. Cross-border humanitarian relief operations are a special arrangement established under specific circumstances; they should be adjusted in a timely manner in light of the developments on the ground, and their ultimate goal should be a transition to cross-line delivery.

Regrettably, the text that was just put to the vote did not address China’s core concerns, nor did it take into account the legitimate concerns of the Syrian Government and other parties. When there were still major differences among Council members, the penholders insisted on pushing for a vote on the draft resolution, which severely undermined the unity and authority of the Security Council. Such an approach is entirely unconstructive. Based on China’s principled position on this issue, China voted against the draft resolution.

China also notes with grave concern that unilateral coercive measures imposed on Syria have severely harmed the economic and social development of Syria and worsened the livelihoods of ordinary Syrian people, compounding the humanitarian crisis. We urge the relevant countries to immediately lift all unilateral coercive measures against Syria.

China stands ready to continue to work with all parties to promote a comprehensive, just and proper political settlement of the Syrian issue and will continue to make its own positive contributions to improving the humanitarian situation in Syria.
after.France:
France deeply regrets the double veto cast today by the Russian Federation and China against a draft resolution supported by 13 members of this Council. 

By opposing this text, which was prepared with exemplary transparency and dedication by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait, Russia and China have chosen to play politics with humanitarian assistance and to obstruct the delivery of vital aid to millions of civilians in dire need. They bear a heavy responsibility before history and before the Syrian people.

The draft resolution before us was purely humanitarian. It responded directly to the urgent appeals of the Secretary-General and the Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs. Today, more than four million people in northern Syria depend on cross-border humanitarian assistance for their daily survival. There is currently no viable alternative to this mechanism to deliver food, medicine, and shelter at the necessary scale, neither in the north-west, where the ongoing offensive by the regime and its allies continues to cause massive displacement and immense suffering, nor in the north-east. 

The co-penholders made considerable efforts to find a compromise, taking into account the concerns expressed by all delegations, including by reducing the number of border crossings from four to three. Thirteen members of this Council recognized those efforts and voted in favour of this balanced, humanitarian compromise. 

The cross-border mechanism authorized by resolution 2165 cannot be replaced by cross-line deliveries from Damascus, which remain arbitrarily obstructed and insufficient. Humanitarian aid must never be instrumentalized or held hostage for political ends. Respect for international humanitarian law is not negotiable; it is an obligation that applies to all.

France warmly thanks Belgium, Germany and Kuwait for their tireless work. We will not abandon the Syrian people. We must continue our collective efforts before the mandate expires on 10 January to ensure that cross-border assistance can continue and that an agreement is found to protect the millions of civilians whose lives depend on our action.
after.Germany:
I speak in my national capacity.

I am devastated by the result of this vote. Today is a sad, dark day for the Security Council, but above all, it is a terrible day for the millions of Syrian civilians who depend on the United Nations for their survival.

For weeks, together with our co-penholders Belgium and Kuwait, we worked tirelessly and transparently to find a compromise that would keep this vital humanitarian lifeline open. We listened carefully to the concerns of all Council members. We showed maximum flexibility, including by agreeing not to seek the reauthorization of the border crossing at Al-Ramtha, reducing the number of border crossings from four to three, and providing for an independent review of cross-line and cross-border operations. We went to the very limit of what was humanitarianly acceptable and operationally responsible. 

The Secretary-General and the United Nations humanitarian agencies have stated time and again, clearly and unequivocally: cross-border aid remains irreplaceable. There is simply no viable alternative to reach millions of vulnerable civilians in north-western and north-eastern Syria, especially as winter sets in and as military operations in Idlib are displacing tens of thousands more civilians as we speak.

Yet, despite all our efforts to preserve a purely humanitarian text focused strictly on saving lives, two permanent members—the Russian Federation and China—decided to cast a veto. By vetoing this draft resolution, they have taken millions of Syrian civilians hostage to political considerations. There is no justification, none whatsoever, for denying food, medicine, and shelter to people in dire need. 

Germany deeply regrets that the Council was prevented today from fulfilling its humanitarian responsibility. We will not give up on the Syrian people. We will continue to work relentlessly with our co-penholders and all Council members to find a solution before the current mandate expires on 10 January.
after.Peru:
(spoke in Spanish): Peru deeply regrets that the draft resolution submitted by Belgium, Germany and Kuwait (S/2019/961) could not be adopted, despite receiving the broad support of the Council. We express our sincere appreciation to the three co-penholders for their tireless, inclusive and transparent efforts to achieve a balanced compromise that responded directly to the urgent humanitarian needs on the ground.

Peru voted in favour of the draft resolution because we firmly believe that the cross-border mechanism authorized by resolution 2165 (2014) remains an indispensable and irreplaceable lifeline for more than four million Syrian civilians. As the Secretary-General and the Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs have consistently underscored, there is currently no viable alternative to this mechanism for delivering vital food, medicine and winterization aid to people in desperate need, particularly in the light of the alarming escalation of hostilities and mass displacement in north-western Syria and the acute humanitarian challenges in the north-east.

We emphasize that humanitarian assistance must be guided strictly by the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and that all parties must comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law, including the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. 

My delegation deeply regrets the persistent division within the Council on this purely humanitarian file. The failure to adopt this resolution prevents the Council from properly fulfilling its primary responsibility and directly jeopardizes the lives of millions of vulnerable people. With the current mandate expiring in only three weeks, we urge all members of the Council to put humanitarian imperatives above political considerations and to redouble their efforts to find a consensus that ensures the uninterrupted delivery of cross-border humanitarian assistance.
after.South Africa:
South Africa voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the co-penholders—Belgium, Germany and Kuwait—as we firmly believe that the Council’s primary responsibility on this issue must be to address the dire humanitarian needs of the Syrian people.

My delegation is deeply disappointed that the Security Council was unable to reach consensus on this critical humanitarian issue today. More than four million people in northern Syria depend on cross-border humanitarian assistance for their basic survival, and the United Nations has consistently reiterated that this mechanism remains an indispensable lifeline, particularly as winter sets in and hostilities continue to displace thousands of vulnerable civilians.

South Africa’s principled vote in favour of the text was guided solely by the imperative to alleviate human suffering and save innocent lives. We believe that humanitarian aid must never be politicized, and that the Council must put the lives and well-being of the Syrian people above political divisions and geopolitical considerations.

At the same time, South Africa reiterates that any humanitarian assistance must fully respect the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and operational independence, as well as the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We have consistently maintained that the cross-border mechanism is an extraordinary and temporary measure, and we encourage increased efforts to expand and scale up cross-line assistance to reach all people in need throughout Syria in cooperation with the relevant authorities.

Finally, we reiterate that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. The only sustainable path to ending the suffering of the Syrian people is through an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process that meets the legitimate aspirations of all its people, in full accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). We urge all Council members to continue to engage constructively and in the spirit of compromise to ensure that life-saving humanitarian assistance continues to reach those who need it most.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted in favour of the draft resolution, and we are deeply disappointed and appalled by the vetoes cast today by the Russian Federation and China. 

We want to express our sincere gratitude to the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Germany and Kuwait—for their tireless efforts, patience and dedication over the past few weeks to achieve a balanced and compromise text. They listened carefully to the concerns of all Council members and made significant concessions to accommodate those concerns, including by reducing the authorized crossings from four to three. Thirteen members of this Council recognized the vital necessity of this resolution and supported it. 

Yet today, Russia and China chose to prioritize their narrow political interests over the lives of millions of vulnerable Syrian civilians. Over four million Syrians in the north rely on cross-border humanitarian assistance for their daily survival—for food, shelter, clean water and medical supplies. In north-western Syria, civilians in Idlib are currently facing an intensified military offensive, relentless bombardment and severe winter conditions. In north-eastern Syria, hundreds of thousands of civilians depend on the Al Yarubiyah crossing for life-saving medicine and surgical supplies that the Syrian regime has consistently blocked from Damascus.

The Secretary-General and the Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs have made it unequivocally clear to this Council: there is no viable alternative to the cross-border mechanism. Cross-line deliveries from Damascus cannot substitute for cross-border operations, because the Assad regime has repeatedly used humanitarian assistance as a weapon of war, systematically denying aid to communities outside its control. 

To veto this resolution today, just days before the mandate expires and in the depths of winter, is unconscionable. It is a cynical, cruel and unjustified act that leaves millions of people wondering whether they will receive the food and medical aid they need to survive. Russia and China have once again chosen to shield a brutal regime rather than protect millions of innocent civilians. 

The United Kingdom will not give up on the Syrian people. We will continue to work closely with the penholders and fellow Council members to ensure that the United Nations cross-border lifeline is preserved before the mandate expires on 10 January.
after.United States of America:
I am in a state of shock. The outcome of today’s vote is nothing short of catastrophic. 

I want to thank the co-penholders—Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait—for their tireless, transparent, and principled efforts over the past several months. They engaged with every member of this Council in good faith to reach a viable compromise, even agreeing to reduce the number of border crossings from four to three in an earnest attempt to accommodate concerns. 

Yet, today, two permanent members of this Council chose to cast a veto against a purely humanitarian resolution. The Russian Federation and China have chosen to play politics with the lives of millions of innocent Syrian civilians. 

Let us be completely clear about what just happened: Russia and China have decided that their allegiance to the murderous Al-Assad regime is more important than ensuring that four million vulnerable Syrian men, women, and children receive food, medicine, and shelter in the dead of winter. There is no viable alternative to the cross-border mechanism. The Secretary-General told us this. The Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs told us this. Every single humanitarian organization operating on the ground told us this. Cross-line assistance alone cannot and will not meet the staggering needs created by the regime's brutal assaults on its own people.

By vetoing this resolution, Russia and China have knowingly chosen to cut off a vital lifeline for millions of human beings. To our Russian and Chinese colleagues: How do you justify this decision? How do you look at the families shivering in Idlib, the mothers trying to keep their infants warm and fed, and tell them that their lives are secondary to shielding a regime that gasses its own citizens and bombs schools and hospitals? The consequences of this vote are devastating, and the blood of those who will suffer and die as a result is on your hands.

The United States voted in favour of this resolution because we believe in basic human dignity and our collective responsibility to alleviate human suffering. We refuse to accept that this Council should simply turn its back on the Syrian people. We will continue to stand firmly with the millions of Syrians in need, and we urge all members of this Council not to rest until a solution is found to ensure the uninterrupted delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance across Syria’s borders.
